**1\. The Problem**

**What is the customer pain or opportunity?**

Saroj is a translator using Paratext 10 Simple. As he works through a normal translation session, he encounters a steady drip of friction: menus, comments, choosing between projects or resources each do not work as expected or are inconsistent. Each irritation is small, but together they leave Saroj feeling that Simple is not ready for work \- Simple isn't yet trustworthy for the field context it is intended to serve.

**Who has this problem?**

Simple users — primarily translators represented here by Saroj. Also affects checkers and admins who move between projects and resources frequently. Not affecting PT10 Power users directly, but the fixes are portable.

**How do we know?**

Internal review by the Simple team, and a defect list compiled from user feedback (menus, comments, project pickers, synced scrolling). 

**What happens if we do nothing?**

Simple continues to feel rough. The team keeps fixing the same defects in three parallel pickers. Field adoption will go poorly because trainers can't confidently point translators at Simple. The gap between Simple's value proposition ("lightweight, focused") and lived experience within it widens.

**2\. Appetite & Boundaries**

**5\. Technical Context**

**Systems involved**

Paratext 10 Simple UI (React); menu system; project picker components in titlebar and modals; comment system; synced-scrolling controller; platform-bible-react (candidate home for shared selector — see existing advanced-project-selector story); S/R server integration for "More projects" affordance.

**Known constraints**

Shared components must not regress PT10 Power (which will eventually adopt them). Performance neutral or better. No breaking changes to Simple's public menu-command API. 

**Open technical questions**

·        Where does the unified multi-select live — platform-bible-react, or a Simple-local shim?

·        Third-column synced scrolling — is this a missing listener, a state-flow issue, or a design tradeoff we chose?

·        "More projects…" — does it open the Home/S/R dialog, expand inline, or push to a separate view?

**1\. The Problem**

**What is the customer pain or opportunity?**

**3\. Shaped Solution**

**How it works**

Six weeks is a coherence pass, not a feature launch. Ship each item as it lands, in this order:

1\.     Week 1 — Menus. Strip out non-Simple items; reorder into a coherent Simple-only structure.

2\.     Week 2 — Copyright copy-paste control \+ Comments improvements (visibility, whitespace, basic filters).

3\.     Weeks 3–4 — Project selection: fix titlebar picker (blue box, "Recent", "Your projects" clarity, "More projects" affordance). Ship in isolation before the unification work.

4\.     Weeks 4–5 — Unified multi-select: extract a shared selector component and adopt it in Simple across Project, Bible text, commentary, text collection, Share layout. Target 2 shared components, not 1\.

5\.     Week 6 — Synced scrolling fix (third column) \+ buffer / defect cleanup.

**Key interactions**

·        Menu open — user sees only Simple-relevant commands, ordered predictably. This is where perception of coherence lives.

·        Project switch — from titlebar, user picks from Recent, Your Projects (now clarified), or opens "More projects…" to reach S/R server projects. This is the highest-frequency decision point.

·        Resource picking (Bible texts, commentaries, text collections) — same UX everywhere. Consistency here is the whole point of the unification work.

**Rabbit holes**

| Rabbit Hole | Why It's Risky | Suggested Approach |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Full unification into one picker component** | Team already flagged "not necessarily 1 UI"; API design across use cases could burn weeks | Target 2 shared components max; accept some divergence |
| **Fixing every reported picker defect** | Long tail: horizontal scroll, modal-over-modal, short-name alignment inconsistencies, More Resources overlap | Fix the top 3 that Saroj hits; punt the rest with a tracking issue |
| **Comments filter parity with PT9** | PT9 has years of filter accretion; matching all of it is a rabbit warren | Ship "basic" filters only; publish an explicit no-go list |
| **Share layout scope creep** | "Share with team" button rewrite is a Nice-to-have that will attract discussion | Only touch Share layout in Week 6 if buffer allows |

 

**4\. Risks**

*Inspired framework: honest read on where this is weakest.*

| Risk Type | Level | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Value — Will users choose to use this?** | **LOW** | These are observed friction points, not speculative features. Value is in the cumulative effect. |
| **Usability — Can users figure it out?** | **LOW** | Every change reduces UI variety or complexity. Risk is inversion of current usability debt. |
| **Feasibility — Can we build it in the appetite?** | **MEDIUM** | Six workstreams in six weeks with 1–2 engineers is tight. Unified selector is the largest unknown. |
| **Viability — Does it work for the business?** | **LOW** | Directly supports PT10 Simple strategic direction and ETEN commitments. |

 

**What discovery have we done (or should we do)?**

Done: session observation with Saroj; internal defect review; roadmap alignment discussion. Recommended before build: (1) a lightweight prototype test of the unified selector with 2–3 translators, (2) a technical spike on the shared selector component architecture, (3) a quick review of the Menu strip-down with the training team so trainers aren't blindsided.

**5\. Technical Context**

**Systems involved**

Paratext 10 Simple UI (React); menu system; project picker components in titlebar and modals; comment system; synced-scrolling controller; platform-bible-react (candidate home for shared selector — see existing advanced-project-selector story); S/R server integration for "More projects" affordance.

**Known constraints**

Shared components must not regress PT10 Power (which will eventually adopt them). Performance neutral or better. No breaking changes to Simple's public menu-command API. Copy-paste control must respect existing copyright handling — do not silently change permission behavior.

**Open technical questions**

·        Where does the unified multi-select live — platform-bible-react, or a Simple-local shim?

·        Third-column synced scrolling — is this a missing listener, a state-flow issue, or a design tradeoff we chose?

·        "More projects…" — does it open the Home/S/R dialog, expand inline, or push to a separate view?

·        Share layout "Share with team" button (if NTH is picked up) — how does it trigger sync without confusing the "Save" affordance?

# **3\. Shaped Solution**

*This is the shaped concept — enough direction to be useful, rough enough to leave room for builders to figure out the details. Think breadboard-level, not pixel-perfect.*

## **How it works**

*Describe the core flow in plain language. Use a simple numbered walkthrough, a rough sketch, or a breadboard diagram. Avoid specifying UI details unless they’re load-bearing.*

## **Key interactions**

*Call out the 2–3 moments that matter most. Where does the user make a decision? Where could they get confused? Where does data flow between systems? Links to key UX mock-ups*

## **Rabbit holes**

*Things that look simple but aren’t. Call these out so the team doesn’t get pulled in.*

 

| \# | Rabbit Hole | Why It’s Risky | Suggested Approach |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
|  | e.g. Syncing state across tabs | Could burn a week on edge cases | Don’t support in v1 — show “refresh” message |
| 1 |  |  |  |

# **4\. Risks**

***Inspired framework:** Every product idea has four categories of risk. Be honest about where this one is weakest.*

 

| Risk Type | Level | Notes |
| :---- | :---: | :---- |
| **Value — Will users choose to use this?** | 🟢  🟡  🔴 |   |
| **Usability — Can users figure it out?** | 🟢  🟡  🔴 |   |
| **Feasibility — Can we build it in the appetite?** | 🟢  🟡  🔴 |   |
| **Viability — Does it work for the business?** | 🟢  🟡  🔴 |   |

 

## **What discovery have we done (or should we do)?**

*Prototype tests, technical spikes, competitor analysis, etc. If you skipped discovery, say why.*

# **5\. Technical Context**

*Just enough for engineering to start thinking — not a spec. The team will fill in the real details during build.*

## **Systems involved**

*List services, databases, APIs, or third-party dependencies that will be touched.*

## **Known constraints**

*Performance requirements, backward compatibility, migration needs, regulatory considerations.*

## **Open technical questions**

*Things the team needs to investigate during build. It’s fine to have these — better to name them than pretend they don’t exist.*

**Changelog**

| Date | Author | What Changed |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
|  Date |  |   |

 

**Template notes:** *This template borrows from two frameworks. [Shape Up](https://basecamp.com/shapeup/1.5-chapter-06) (Basecamp) contributes appetite over estimates, fixed-time/variable-scope, shaping before building, rabbit holes, and no-gos. [Inspired](https://www.svpg.com/books/inspired-how-to-create-tech-products-customers-love-2nd-edition/) (Marty Cagan) contributes the focus on outcomes over outputs, the four-risk framework, and the emphasis on discovery before delivery. The goal is a document light enough to actually get written, specific enough to align a team, and honest enough to surface risks early.*
